{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Convex minimization with higher-order Hölder regularity in normed geometry: full-space queries\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}HO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}HOC07\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}full}

Single-objective optimization

Solve \AtlasInlineMath{\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)} to obtain an objective-value approximation relative to the global infimum.

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Global minimization; task family: Single objective

\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; geometry: Full space; geometry: Norm ball; smoothness: Kth derivative holder

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} access order: Higher-order interface; feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Full jet; operation: Exact jet k; public information: Computable access; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Known upper bound; public information: Known exact value; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic algorithms; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; feasibility: Required; object: Point; postprocessing: Unqueried output explicitly allowed

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Objective gap

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; mode: Deterministic; mode: Probability; randomness: Algorithm private seed

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: Oracle calls; precision: Bit precision not counted

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Solve \AtlasInlineMath{\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)} to obtain an objective-value approximation relative to the global infimum.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The objective \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}} is convex and \AtlasInlineMath{C^k}.

There exists a global minimizer \AtlasInlineMath{x^*} satisfying \AtlasInlineMath{\|x^*-x_0\|_p\le R}.


\AtlasMath{\|D^{k}f(x)-D^{k}f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op},p}\le M_{k,\nu}\|x-y\|_{p}^{\nu}.}


Fix \AtlasInlineMath{k\ge2} and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\nu\le1}; the tensor norm is induced by the stated vector norm. Finite norm exponents satisfy \AtlasInlineMath{1\le p<\infty}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Each query selects \AtlasInlineMath{x} in \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d} and returns the complete exact tuple \AtlasInlineMath{J_{k}f(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^{k}f(x))}. The fixed objective uniquely determines the response, with no stochastic noise.

The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{x_0}, the target accuracy, and \AtlasInlineMath{d}, \AtlasInlineMath{k}, \AtlasInlineMath{M_{k,\nu}}, \AtlasInlineMath{\nu}, \AtlasInlineMath{R}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_f}, \AtlasInlineMath{p}. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d}.

The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base error is


\AtlasMath{\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=f(\widehat{x})-f^*.}


Here \AtlasInlineMath{f^*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)}. The lower-boundedness or attainment assumption makes this error finite and nonnegative.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Each primitive response specified under ORACLE costs one unit. Queries at new points introduced by any inner procedure also count toward the total.

The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.

Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic}
Arbitrary measurable adaptive deterministic algorithms are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.


\AtlasMath{f(\widehat{x})-f^*\le \varepsilon_f.}


The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized}
Arbitrary measurable adaptive algorithms with private randomness are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.


\AtlasMath{\Pr\!\left[f(\widehat{x})-f^*\le \varepsilon_f\right]\ge\frac23.}


Expectation or probability is evaluated after fixing the instance; randomness comes from the algorithm's private random seed.

The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{x,\widehat{x},x_0}: Query or decision point, algorithm output, and public initial point. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}: Real coordinate space; vectors use the Euclidean norm unless otherwise stated. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d} is a positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{\langle u,v\rangle,\ \|u\|_2}: Euclidean inner product and norm.


\AtlasMath{\langle u,v\rangle=u^\top v,\qquad\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{D^jf(x),\ \nabla f(x),\ \nabla^2f(x)}: Fréchet derivative of order \AtlasInlineMath{j}, gradient and Hessian. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{j\in\{0,\ldots,k\}} and \AtlasInlineMath{D^0f=f}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}},\ \|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}}: Induced operator norm of a Euclidean multilinear tensor; the spectral norm for matrices.


\AtlasMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|.}


\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{E}}: Base error defined in the metric specification; expectation or probability aggregation is imposed by the guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N}: Total number of original oracle calls; the unit cost is specified in the resource convention. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{T^*}: Minimum worst-case budget for one algorithm to meet the requirement on the full instance class, within the specified regime, guarantee and resource projection. Expected-resource specifications instead minimize the per-instance expected budget.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}}: Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching bounds up to constants, and upper bounds omitting the declared logarithmic factors. \textbf{Domain:} Hidden constants, fixed parameters, and omitted logarithmic variables are specified for each bound.

\AtlasInlineMath{\inf,\sup,\min,\max}: Infimum, supremum, attained minimum and attained maximum.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C}: Positive universal constants without assigned numerical values; a subscript permits dependence only on the indicated fixed parameters. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c,C<\infty}.

\AtlasInlineMath{J_{k}f(x)}: Function value and the complete tuple of derivatives from order one through the specified maximum order.


\AtlasMath{J_{k}f(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^{k}f(x)).}


\AtlasInlineMath{f,f^*}: Unknown objective and its global infimum over the specified feasible domain.


\AtlasMath{f^*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x).}


\AtlasInlineMath{\|x\|_p,\ \|x\|_\infty}: Finite-exponent vector norms and the maximum-coordinate norm.


\AtlasMath{\|x\|_p=\left(\sum_{i=1}^d|x_i|^p\right)^{1/p},\qquad\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|.}


\AtlasInlineMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op},p}}: Replace every Euclidean unit ball in the tensor operator-norm definition by the \AtlasInlineMath{\ell_p} unit ball; define \AtlasInlineMath{p=\infty} analogously.

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension; dimension requirements are stated separately for each bound. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb{N}_{+}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{k}: Maximum order of the query interface and Taylor model; this integer is fixed before other parameters are compared. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{k\in\mathbb{N}, k\ge2}.

\AtlasInlineMath{M_{k,\nu}}: Global \AtlasInlineMath{\nu}-Hölder upper bound for the order-\AtlasInlineMath{k} derivative in the specified tensor norm. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{M_{k,\nu}\ge0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\nu}: Hölder exponent of the highest derivative \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\nu\le1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{s}: Sum of the highest derivative order and its Hölder exponent. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{s>2}.


\AtlasMath{s=k+\nu.}


\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Upper bound on the distance from the known initial point to at least one global minimizer. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R\ge0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_f}: Objective-gap tolerance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_f>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{p}: Finite norm exponent of the vector space. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{1\le p<\infty}.

\AtlasInlineMath{p^*}: Conjugate norm exponent.


\AtlasMath{p^*=\frac{p}{p-1}\ (p>1),\qquad p^*=\infty\ (p=1).}


\AtlasInlineMath{m_p}: Auxiliary exponent determined by the norm geometry. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{m_p\ge2}.


\AtlasMath{m_p=\max\{2,p\}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{a_p}: High-order complexity exponent for the corresponding norm geometry. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{a_p>0}.


\AtlasMath{a_p=\frac{m_p}{(m_p+1)\,s-(m_p)}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{a}: Complexity exponent associated with the highest-order regularity. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{a>0}.


\AtlasMath{a=\frac{2}{3\,s-(2)}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{C_{k,\nu,p}}: Sufficient window constants depending only on the fixed orders or exponents in their subscripts; existence is asserted without numerical values. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{C_{k,\nu,p}>1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{Q}}: Dimensionless ratio formed from the highest-order regularity, radius, and target accuracy; distinct from the feasible set \AtlasInlineMath{Q}. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{Q}\ge0}.


\AtlasMath{\mathcal{Q}=\frac{M_{k,\nu}\,(R)^{s}}{\varepsilon_f}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E},\Pr}: Expectation and probability after fixing the instance; their randomness sources are specified by the guarantee.

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy For \$N\textbackslash{}ge2\$,\allowbreak{} define\newline{}\$\$h\_\allowbreak{}N(z)=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}frac1s\textbackslash{}left(\textbackslash{}sum\_\allowbreak{}\{i=\allowbreak{}1\}\textasciicircum{}\{N-1\}|z\_\allowbreak{}i-z\_\allowbreak{}\{i+1\}|\textasciicircum{}s+|z\_\allowbreak{}N|\textasciicircum{}s\textbackslash{}right)-z\_\allowbreak{}1.\$\$\newline{}Let \$A\$ be the forward-difference matrix with a terminal row. Its Euclidean operator norm is at most two. The first \$k\$ derivatives of \$|u|\textasciicircum{}s/\allowbreak{}s\$ vanish at zero,\allowbreak{} and its kth derivative has a \$\textbackslash{}nu\$-H{\AtlasUnicodeText ö}\allowbreak{}lder modulus depending only on \$k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\$. Applying H{\AtlasUnicodeText ö}\allowbreak{}lder's inequality with exponents \$s/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu,\allowbreak{}s,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}ldots,\allowbreak{}s\$ gives\newline{}\$\$|[D\textasciicircum{}kh\_\allowbreak{}N(z)-D\textasciicircum{}kh\_\allowbreak{}N(w)][u\_\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}ldots,\allowbreak{}u\_\allowbreak{}k]|\newline{}\textbackslash{}le H\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\textbackslash{}|z-w\textbackslash{}|\_\allowbreak{}2\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}nu\textbackslash{}prod\_\allowbreak{}j\textbackslash{}|u\_\allowbreak{}j\textbackslash{}|\_\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{}\$\$\newline{}with \$H\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$ independent of \$N\$.\newline{}\newline{}The minimizer is \$z\textasciicircum{}*=\allowbreak{}(N,\allowbreak{}N-1,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}ldots,\allowbreak{}1)\$,\allowbreak{} with\newline{}\$\$h\_\allowbreak{}N(0)-h\_\allowbreak{}N(z\textasciicircum{}*)=\allowbreak{}(s-1)N/\allowbreak{}s,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad\newline{}\textbackslash{}|z\textasciicircum{}*\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2=\allowbreak{}N(N+1)(2N+1)/\allowbreak{}6.\$\$\newline{}If \$z\_\allowbreak{}\{t+1\}=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}cdots=\allowbreak{}z\_\allowbreak{}N=\allowbreak{}0\$,\allowbreak{} then the remaining chain gives\newline{}\$\$h\_\allowbreak{}N(z)-h\_\allowbreak{}N(z\textasciicircum{}*)\textbackslash{}ge(s-1)(N-t)/\allowbreak{}s,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad\newline{}\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla h\_\allowbreak{}N(z)\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}ge1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sqrt\{t+1\}.\$\$\newline{}For the gradient inequality,\allowbreak{} the first \$t+1\$ gradient coordinates sum to \$-1\$,\allowbreak{} and Cauchy{\AtlasUnicodeText –}\allowbreak{}Schwarz applies.\newline{}\newline{}For any deterministic adaptive algorithm making \$T\$ queries,\allowbreak{} select orthonormal chain directions successively,\allowbreak{} orthogonal to previous directions and the query displacements seen so far. Vanishing derivatives of unrevealed terms ensure that each complete jet exposes at most the next direction. After the output is determined,\allowbreak{} choose the remaining hidden directions orthogonal to that output too. The sufficient dimension \$d\textbackslash{}ge N+T+1\$ leaves room for these choices. The final function\newline{}\$\$f(x)=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}alpha h\_\allowbreak{}N(V\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}top(x-x\_\allowbreak{}0)/\allowbreak{}b)\$\$\newline{}is one fixed admissible instance consistent with the entire transcript. This construction does not select a separate instance after seeing a randomized algorithm's private seed.\newline{}\newline{}For a radius promise,\allowbreak{} take \$b=\allowbreak{}R/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}|z\textasciicircum{}*\textbackslash{}|\$ and \$\textbackslash{}alpha=\allowbreak{}M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}b\textasciicircum{}s/\allowbreak{}H\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$. Choosing \$N=\allowbreak{}2T+2\$ for objective gap or \$N=\allowbreak{}T+2\$ for gradient norm gives\newline{}\$\$\textbackslash{}operatorname\{gap\}(T)\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}frac\{c\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}R\textasciicircum{}s\}\{(T+1)\textasciicircum{}\{(3s-2)/\allowbreak{}2\}\},\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad\newline{}\textbackslash{}operatorname\{grad\}\_\allowbreak{}R(T)\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}frac\{c\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}R\textasciicircum{}\{s-1\}\}\{(T+1)\textasciicircum{}\{(3s-2)/\allowbreak{}2\}\}.\$\$\newline{}For an initial-gap promise,\allowbreak{} set \$\textbackslash{}alpha=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}Delta s/\allowbreak{}((s-1)N)\$ and \$b=\allowbreak{}(\textbackslash{}alpha H\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}/\allowbreak{}M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\})\textasciicircum{}\{1/\allowbreak{}s\}\$. Then\newline{}\$\$\textbackslash{}operatorname\{grad\}\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}Delta(T)\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}frac\{c\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\textasciicircum{}\{1/\allowbreak{}s\}\textbackslash{}Delta\textasciicircum{}\{(s-1)/\allowbreak{}s\}\}\{(T+1)\textasciicircum{}\{(3s-2)/\allowbreak{}(2s)\}\}.\$\$\newline{}Inverting these inequalities yields the linked bounds with a sufficient dimension proportional to one plus the complexity scale. The minimizer lies in the localization ball,\allowbreak{} so the same hard subclass is admissible for ball-restricted optimization.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy For a full-space differentiable objective with \$f(x\_\allowbreak{}0)-\textbackslash{}inf f\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} the condition \$\textbackslash{}Delta=\allowbreak{}0\$ makes \$x\_\allowbreak{}0\$ a global minimizer. Its gradient is zero,\allowbreak{} and its Hessian is positive semidefinite whenever it exists. Thus first-order and spectral second-order stationarity require no query. An objective-gap target also requires no query when \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon\_\allowbreak{}f\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}Delta\$. Nonnegative query cost proves exact optimality of these zero bounds.\newline{}\newline{}If a public gradient-Lipschitz bound \$\textbackslash{}beta\$ is part of the specification,\allowbreak{} the descent lemma gives \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x\_\allowbreak{}0)\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}le2\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta\$. For convex full-space objectives with a minimizer within distance \$R\$,\allowbreak{} it also gives \$f(x\_\allowbreak{}0)-f\textasciicircum{}*\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}beta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2\$ and \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x\_\allowbreak{}0)\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}beta R\$. These sufficient zero-query regions require that explicit first-order regularity assumption. If only the highest derivative is controlled,\allowbreak{} positive quadratics can have arbitrary curvature and arbitrarily large initial gap despite zero highest-order modulus.\newline{}\newline{}On a connected Euclidean domain,\allowbreak{} \$M\_\allowbreak{}k=\allowbreak{}0\$ or \$M\_\allowbreak{}\{k,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}=\allowbreak{}0\$ makes \$D\textasciicircum{}kf\$ constant,\allowbreak{} so \$f\$ is a polynomial of degree at most \$k\$. One complete jet determines all coefficients. Under the specified free internal computation,\allowbreak{} a known polynomial can then be optimized on a compact public domain,\allowbreak{} or combined with a public regularizer and solved through the declared known-model interface.\newline{}\newline{}A bounded-below polynomial on the full space need not attain its infimum. For approximate spectral stationarity,\allowbreak{} shift \$x\_\allowbreak{}0\$ to zero and minimize \$f(x)+\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}|x\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2\$. This function is coercive,\allowbreak{} and its minimizer \$x\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}eta\$ satisfies \$\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}|x\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}eta)\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}Delta\}\$,\allowbreak{} and \$\textbackslash{}nabla\textasciicircum{}2f(x\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}eta)\textbackslash{}succeq-\textbackslash{}eta I\$. Choosing \$\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{\textbackslash{}varepsilon\_\allowbreak{}H,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\_\allowbreak{}g\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}Delta)\textbackslash{}\}\$ meets both targets. For global objective accuracy,\allowbreak{} exact polynomial coefficients permit arbitrary-accuracy internal global optimization;\allowbreak{} no additional unknown-function query is needed.\newline{}\newline{}To exclude zero queries in a nontrivial region,\allowbreak{} choose two positive quadratics centered on opposite sides of \$x\_\allowbreak{}0\$,\allowbreak{} with the same public budgets and disjoint acceptable-output sets. A zero-query algorithm has the same output distribution on both instances,\allowbreak{} so their success probabilities sum to at most one. It cannot succeed with probability at least \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$ on each. With only highest-order regularity,\allowbreak{} curvature can be increased until the acceptable sets are disjoint at any prescribed positive accuracy and positive localization radius. In an initial-gap model with additional curvature restrictions,\allowbreak{} retain the bound's explicit accuracy and compatibility window.\newline{}\newline{}If both a global PL constant \$\textbackslash{}mu\$ and a gradient-Lipschitz upper bound \$\textbackslash{}beta\$ are supplied,\allowbreak{} then \$2\textbackslash{}mu(f-f\_\allowbreak{}*)\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}le2\textbackslash{}beta(f-f\_\allowbreak{}*)\$. When \$\textbackslash{}mu>\textbackslash{}beta>0\$,\allowbreak{} every gap is zero and the class contains only constant objectives. This degeneracy does not apply without the extra \$\textbackslash{}beta\$ assumption.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Retained premises:\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}common\_\allowbreak{}specification (59c0726f7ecbd97a7790da4a305ad361206a8f196e5c2054ec025b5f48ba19da),\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}views/\allowbreak{}1 (873400a618391c5f34909dcf88fc74ed8a4171d0eb99793f280fd666407a1bbd),\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}quantities/\allowbreak{}3 (e98d41b2d6b04dc44923b7282c5370210ad87a839c73cc1b7593686549b8f74a),\allowbreak{} and /\allowbreak{}proofs/\allowbreak{}1 (b4cae642401d5d94cdce40203762dbe2dcc36171225cbeaa38b31ba59414bf25). No external theorem is introduced.\newline{}LOWER:\allowbreak{} Fix public parameters with R>0. Let a\_\allowbreak{}plus=\allowbreak{}x0+R e1 and a\_\allowbreak{}minus=\allowbreak{}x0-R e1,\allowbreak{} and f\_\allowbreak{}plus/\allowbreak{}minus(x)=\allowbreak{}A||x-a\_\allowbreak{}plus/\allowbreak{}minus||\_\allowbreak{}2\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} where A>epsilon\_\allowbreak{}f/\allowbreak{}R\textasciicircum{}2. Both objectives are convex C\textasciicircum{}infinity,\allowbreak{} have a minimizer at lp-distance R,\allowbreak{} and have constant kth derivative for k=\allowbreak{}2 or zero kth derivative for k>2. Thus their kth-derivative Holder modulus is zero and is admissible under any public upper bound M. Their epsilon\_\allowbreak{}f-optimal sets are disjoint Euclidean balls of radius sqrt(epsilon\_\allowbreak{}f/\allowbreak{}A)<R. Without a query the output distribution is identical for both objectives,\allowbreak{} so its probabilities of belonging to these disjoint sets sum to at most one. It cannot succeed with probability at least 2/\allowbreak{}3 for each fixed instance. Oracle counts are integers,\allowbreak{} so every worst-path budget B<1 permits zero queries and fails;\allowbreak{} C*>=\allowbreak{}1.\newline{}TAYLOR:\allowbreak{} At a queried point c let T\_\allowbreak{}c(x)=\allowbreak{}sum\_\allowbreak{}\{j=\allowbreak{}0\}\textasciicircum{}k D\textasciicircum{}j f(c)[x-c]\textasciicircum{}j/\allowbreak{}j!. For h=\allowbreak{}x-c,\allowbreak{} repeated integration along c+t h gives f(c+h)-T\_\allowbreak{}c(c+h)=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}(k-1)! integral\_\allowbreak{}0\textasciicircum{}1 (1-t)\textasciicircum{}(k-1) (D\textasciicircum{}k f(c+t h)-D\textasciicircum{}k f(c))[h,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}h] dt. Consequently |f(c+h)-T\_\allowbreak{}c(c+h)| <=\allowbreak{} M||h||\_\allowbreak{}p\textasciicircum{}(k+nu)/\allowbreak{}k! <=\allowbreak{} M||h||\_\allowbreak{}p\textasciicircum{}s/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} because t\textasciicircum{}nu<=\allowbreak{}1 and k>=\allowbreak{}2. If a known compact set K contains a global minimizer and is contained in B\_\allowbreak{}p(c,\allowbreak{}r),\allowbreak{} select a global minimizer y of the known polynomial T\_\allowbreak{}c on K. Existence follows from continuity and compactness;\allowbreak{} the declared free internal operations permit its selection without another unknown-function response. The two remainder inequalities and T\_\allowbreak{}c(y)<=\allowbreak{}T\_\allowbreak{}c(x*) give f(y)-f*<=\allowbreak{}M r\textasciicircum{}s. All lower-order derivatives,\allowbreak{} even when arbitrarily large,\allowbreak{} are included exactly in T\_\allowbreak{}c.\newline{}SATURATION:\allowbreak{} Query at x0 and use K=\allowbreak{}B\_\allowbreak{}p(x0,\allowbreak{}R). The localization promise puts x* in K,\allowbreak{} hence error<=\allowbreak{}M R\textasciicircum{}s. Thus Q=\allowbreak{}M R\textasciicircum{}s/\allowbreak{}epsilon\_\allowbreak{}f<=\allowbreak{}1 suffices for one query in every dimension. Together with LOWER,\allowbreak{} C*=\allowbreak{}1. Q=\allowbreak{}1 is included by a non-strict inequality. This is a sufficient threshold,\allowbreak{} not a claimed maximal one-query domain.\newline{}ONE DIMENSION:\allowbreak{} Every finite lp norm equals absolute value. Set n=\allowbreak{}1+ceil(log2(max\{1,\allowbreak{}Q\})/\allowbreak{}s). Begin with I=\allowbreak{}[x0-R,\allowbreak{}x0+R],\allowbreak{} which contains a global minimizer. For the first n-1 queries,\allowbreak{} query the midpoint c. If f'(c)=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{} convexity makes c globally optimal and return it. If f'(c)>0 keep the left closed half;\allowbreak{} if f'(c)<0 keep the right closed half. Convexity preserves a global minimizer in the retained interval,\allowbreak{} including possible endpoint minimizers. Unless already terminated,\allowbreak{} the nth query is the midpoint of the current pre-cut interval,\allowbreak{} whose radius is r=\allowbreak{}R*2\textasciicircum{}(-(n-1)). Minimize that query's known Taylor polynomial on that interval and return its minimizer without an extra oracle query. Its error is at most M r\textasciicircum{}s<=\allowbreak{}epsilon\_\allowbreak{}f because Q*2\textasciicircum{}(-s(n-1))<=\allowbreak{}1. Total responses on every path are at most n. All query choices and a fixed measurable minimizer selection depend only on public inputs and received jets. The deterministic success guarantee implies success probability one in the randomized view,\allowbreak{} with the identical fixed-path cost.\newline{}BOUNDARIES:\allowbreak{} R=\allowbreak{}0 remains the separate zero-query q2 endpoint,\allowbreak{} and M=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}R>0 remains the separate polynomial-recovery q2 endpoint. This proof neither transfers q2/\allowbreak{}q3 bounds to q1 nor uses a randomized resisting rotation.\par\endgroup
